table_title: List the 10 largest sauropod dinosaurs ranked by estimated body mass per Wikipedia's `Largest and heaviest animals` master article's 'Table of the largest sauropods', with Rank (1-10 by mass DESC), Estimated mass in tonnes (range cell — sauropod mass estimates are inherently range-bound due to fragmentary fossil record), and Estimated total length in m + ft (compound range cell). Universe per cycle-1 audit's BLOCKING pivot: the originally proposed master 'List of largest dinosaurs' redirects to 'Dinosaur size' which is cleanup-flagged for outdated/unreliable overestimates and is prose/range-based rather than deterministic top-N table; the cleanest Wikipedia table is 'Table of the largest sauropods' in 'Largest and heaviest animals' article — sauropod-only mass-ranked closed 10-row table. Per cycle-1 audit SUGGESTION: Animal PK uses source-table verbatim labels including slash-combined rows ('Maraapunisaurus fragillimus/Amphicoelias fragilimus' = name change controversy in paleontology; 'Barosaurus lentus/Supersaurus vivianae BYU 9024' = specimen-level identification ambiguity). Estimate columns kept as text (NOT numeric central values) per cycle-1 audit SUGGESTION because sauropod mass + length estimates are inherently range-bound; single-central-value extraction would NOT be source-extractive.
db_analog: SELECT animal_name, rank, estimated_mass_tonnes_range, estimated_total_length_m_ft_compound FROM wiki_largest_heaviest_animals_largest_sauropods_table ORDER BY rank ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `Largest and heaviest animals` master article's 'Table of the largest sauropods', accessed via cycle-1 audit's master-derived 10-row dump on 2026-05-20. Universe is the closed canonical 10-entry sauropod mass-ranked table — NOT the broader 'List of largest dinosaurs' (redirects to 'Dinosaur size' which is cleanup-flagged + prose/range-based, NOT deterministic top-N) NOR all-dinosaurs by body length (mass-ranked is the master's native ranking convention; body length is shown alongside but not the ranking axis). source_count = 1 registered (Wikipedia `Largest and heaviest animals` article — universe + value role for all 4 cells per master's compound 4-column table). Per cycle-1 audit's 3 BLOCKING fixes: (1) source pivot from 'List of largest dinosaurs' (redirects to cleanup-flagged 'Dinosaur size') to 'Largest and heaviest animals' compound table; (2) estimate-range columns kept as text (NOT numeric central values) — sauropod mass + length estimates are inherently uncertainty-bound per fragmentary fossil record; (3) instance renamed `largest_dinosaurs_by_body_length` → `largest_sauropods_by_estimated_mass` reflecting the master's actual scope (sauropod-only) + native ranking axis (mass DESC, not length DESC — Barosaurus/Supersaurus has largest length range but rank 5 by mass). Per-row cells: Animal name verbatim from source table including slash-combined entries (Maraapunisaurus fragillimus/Amphicoelias fragilimus reflects 2018 genus reclassification debate; Barosaurus lentus/Supersaurus vivianae BYU 9024 reflects specimen-level taxonomic uncertainty); Rank integer 1-10; Estimated mass [tonnes] text range with en-dash separator ('110–170', '80–120', etc.); Estimated total length [m (ft)] compound format with metric primary + imperial parenthetical with en-dashes for both ('44.1–45 (144.6–148)'). temporal_sensitivity = low — fossil discoveries can update rankings infrequently. Cycle-1 audit's master-derived 10-row dump used verbatim at cycle-0 staging.
_extraction_notes: Comparative instance — closed canonical 10-entry largest-sauropods mass-ranked universe per Wikipedia `Largest and heaviest animals` master article's compound table. Single PK Animal (10 closed values including slash-combined entries reflecting taxonomic uncertainty). NEW `taxonomic-entities/dinosaurs` fine-class extending taxonomic-entities bucket from 5 to 6 instances (joining moons, species, nutrients, stars, asteroids). NEW `Science/Paleontology` subdomain — no paleontology in pkdb_bench previously (closest neighbors: Science/Astronomy, Science/Chemistry, Science/Geology). Source plan: 1 registered source (Wikipedia `Largest and heaviest animals` article master — universe + value role for all 4 cells per cycle-1 audit's compound-table dump). claim_type = source_defined per cycle-1 audit confirmation; cycle-1 BLOCKING-fix #2 retains source_defined cleanly by keeping estimate columns as text ranges (NOT curator-judgment central values). Cycle arc: 1 round of pre-staging design review (cycle-1 'Revise' with 3 BLOCKING + 2 SUGGESTION — source pivot from List of largest dinosaurs to Largest and heaviest animals + estimate-cell text-range convention + scope rename to sauropods-by-mass; ID rename `largest_dinosaurs_by_body_length` → `largest_sauropods_by_estimated_mass`; SUGGESTION-1: text ranges not numeric centrals; SUGGESTION-2: Animal PK verbatim including slash-combined rows). All cycle-1 fixes applied at cycle-0 staging using audit's verbatim 10-row dump. 4-cell schema (Animal PK + Rank + Estimated mass + Estimated total length) at 10 rows = 40 source-grounded cell values. Sort: Rank ASC (= Mass DESC per master native ordering). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable include Argentinosaurus huinculensis (often cited as 'largest dinosaur ever'), Patagotitan mayorum (2014 Patagonian discovery), Diplodocus relatives, Mamenchisaurus (long-necked Chinese sauropod); mid-difficulty include Sauroposeidon, Dreadnoughtus schrani (2014 Argentinian discovery); harder calibration include Bruhathkayosaurus matleyi rank #1 at 110–170 tonnes (Indian fossil with controversial size estimates — some paleontologists doubt the 1989 measurements), Maraapunisaurus fragillimus / Amphicoelias fragilimus slash-name reflecting 2018 genus-reclassification debate, Notocolossus gonzalezparejasi (lesser-known 2016 description), Barosaurus lentus / Supersaurus vivianae BYU 9024 slash-entry reflecting specimen-level taxonomic uncertainty (BYU 9024 specimen tentatively assigned). Comparative category-fit: per the comparative category contract, the row universe is filtered to top-N by a numeric ranking attribute (Mass tonnes range — used as ordinal via the source-provided Rank column). Mirror precedent for comparative + closed-canonical universe + range-cell convention: `largest_asteroids_with_geometric_mean_diameter_above_250_km` (numeric threshold but central diameter cells); `uiaa_recognized_eight_thousanders` (closed canonical Wikipedia table). The text-range convention here is novel — first pkdb_bench instance to keep estimate cells as text ranges (NOT central numeric values) per source-extractive integrity when source itself publishes ranges.
